nodes.description: The majority of osteopetrosis cases result from mutations in genes required for acidification of the osteoclast resorption lacuna. TCIRG1 encodes the a3 subunit of the vacuolar proton pump (V-ATPase), and its loss prevents acid secretion into the resorption lacuna. CLCN7 encodes a chloride-proton antiporter that provides the chloride conductance needed to maintain electroneutrality during proton pumping. OSTM1 stabilizes CLCN7. Without adequate acidification, hydroxyapatite dissolution fails and bone matrix cannot be degraded, leading to progressive accumulation of unresorbed primary spongiosa.

nodes.description: A subset of ARO cases result from mutations in TNFSF11 (encoding RANKL) or TNFRSF11A (encoding RANK), which are essential for osteoclast differentiation from monocyte-macrophage precursors. These osteoclast-poor forms lack mature osteoclasts entirely. In TNFSF11 (RANKL) deficiency, the defect lies in the bone microenvironment (osteoblasts fail to produce RANKL), so HSCT does not correct the phenotype. In contrast, TNFRSF11A (RANK) mutations affect the hematopoietic osteoclast precursors themselves, so HSCT can theoretically provide functional RANK-expressing donor monocytes.

nodes.description: A third route to osteoclast-rich osteopetrosis, distinct from both the acidification defect and the osteoclast-poor differentiation defect. PLEKHM1 couples RAB7-positive late endosomal and lysosomal vesicles to the osteoclast plasma membrane, and SNX10 acts in the same vesicular trafficking step. When either is lost the osteoclast differentiates normally but fails to build a ruffled border, so the secretory machinery never reaches the bone-facing membrane and resorption fails despite intact proton-pumping capacity. This is the mechanistic route behind the relatively mild, intermediate course that most reported PLEKHM1 and SNX10 cases follow.

nodes.description: LRRK1 is a leucine-rich repeat kinase that phosphorylates and activates the small GTPases RAC1 and CDC42 in the osteoclast within minutes of RANKL stimulation. Loss of LRRK1 kinase function leaves RAC1/CDC42 underphosphorylated and inactive and the osteoclast unable to resorb, and expressing a constitutively active RAC1 partially restores resorption. In humans this produces osteosclerotic metaphyseal dysplasia, in which the sclerosis is concentrated at the metaphyses and epiphyseal margins rather than being generalised.
